Title.rationale: `public override string Title` appends `+{FakeUpgradeLevel}` to the card name (Wither.cs:16-27) so a fake-upgraded Wither reads "Wither+2". Presentation -- the sim has no card-title layer -- but worth recording because it is the only `Title` override in the pool and it exists precisely because FakeUpgrade does not touch `CurrentUpgradeLevel`.

MaxUpgradeLevel.rationale: `=> 0` (Wither.cs:42) == the class attribute, and it is what forces the fake-upgrade mechanism to exist: Wither can never be really upgraded, so Aeonglass grows it through a side channel.

CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Unplayable }` (Wither.cs:46) == `is_playable = False`. No Ethereal and no Exhaust, so Wither stays in hand and keeps hurting every turn.

ctor.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): `Card.energy_cost` (`sts2_rl/cards/base.py`) now short-circuits on `self._energy_cost < 0` as its first check, returning the raw canonical value before consulting `_free_this_turn` / `_cost_this_turn` / `_cost_this_combat` / `_cost_delta_this_turn` -- mirrors `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers`'s `if (_base < 0) return num;` short-circuit (`CardEnergyCost.cs:101-104`; the record's `:100-103` cite is one line of decompiler drift), which runs before any local or global modifier. All 29 unplayable curse/status/quest cards now set `self._energy_cost = -1` in `_init_vars` (previously 0), each verified individually against its own C# `base(-1, CardType.X, ...)` constructor -- no exceptions, no ascension-gated cost variant. Readers audit (every non-cards/ `energy_cost` hit read in context): combat play/auto-play/valid_actions/action-mask sites gate on `is_playable` first and never see -1; every global-modifier site routes through `hooks.modify_card_energy_cost`, whose dispatcher ends `return max(0, cost)` -- the sim's analogue of C#'s `Math.Max(0, GetWithModifiers(...))` in `GetAmountToSpend`/`GetResolved` (`CardEnergyCost.cs:134-141`) -- so what is SPENT and what the observation encoder reads (`full_env.py` card_features via `previews.py` preview_card_energy_cost) are byte-for-byte unchanged. The three previously-known readers (`relics/mummified_hand.py`, `potions.py` TouchOfInsanity, `cards/event_cards.py` Enlightenment) remain correct, confirmed by unit tests. NOT closed here: `selectors.py`'s `scripted_card_selector` 'to_draw_top' purpose (Headbutt/Thinking Ahead) ranks by raw `card.energy_cost` unclamped -- a sim-only heuristic with no C# analogue; a curse in a Headbutt-eligible discard pile now ranks below-cost instead of tying at 0. No test exercises it; filed in GAP-QUEUE.md's 'Named work with no entry of its own'. New pins: test/test_unplayable_cost.py (15 tests).  The text it replaced read: STATUS / STATUS / NONE map exactly. The canonical energy cost is -1 in C# and 0 in the sim. `CardEnergyCost.GetWithModifiers` returns early on `_base < 0` (CardEnergyCost.cs:100-103), so the game's unplayable card is immune to every cost modifier; the sim runs a base of 0 through the full modifier chain (cards/base.py:222-232). Only what is READ diverges. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/ascenders_bane's ctor entry (rule 3). DORMANT: every ported cost reader filters `> 0` or skips `<= 1`, and events/infested_automaton.py:35 filters pool_card_ids(), which holds no curses or statuses.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: the base 3 lives in the `_BASE_DAMAGE` class constant and a `damage` property (wither.py:157, 163-165)
CanonicalVars.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 24.) All 23 cards now store their printed C# var under a `_`-attribute (or, for 3 cards whose C# var is a live/computed value at display time -- guilty, normality, expect_a_fight -- a `magic_number` property override; wither similarly overrides `base_damage`) so `Card.base_damage`/`base_block`/`base_hp_loss`/`magic_number` report the C# value instead of the 0/None default. Two additive base.py changes: `_frail` added to `_MAGIC_ATTRS` (shame) and a new `base_gold` property (debt, spoils_map -- GoldVar had no base property at all). feel_no_pain's `_block` was renamed to `_power_amount` (fixing a WRONG value, not just a missing one -- `base_block` no longer misreports it as block-granting; matches Rage/Corruption/Stampede's DynamicVar('Power', ...) convention). Combat behavior / dealt numbers are byte-identical in every case -- a printed-number / observation-encoder fix only. 3 of the 23 (debt, spoils_map, rolling_boulder's secondary IncrementAmount) have NO obs-vector change despite the API fix (full_env.py has no base_gold read site; magic_number carries one number per card and _power_amount dominates rolling_boulder's scan) -- documented, not closed further. CHECKPOINT NOTE for training: encoded VALUES changed for the other 20 cards in feature slots f[17]/f[18] damage, f[20]/f[21] block, f[22] hp_loss, f[23] magic_number; obs LAYOUT unchanged. Pins: test/test_printed_vars.py (48 tests).  The text it replaced read: `new DamageVar(3m, ValueProp.Unpowered | ValueProp.Move)` (Wither.cs:44) is the printed damage, and the SIM'S ARITHMETIC IS RIGHT: C# grows it by mutating the var (`DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` inside `FakeUpgrade`, Wither.cs:65) while the sim recomputes it as `_BASE_DAMAGE + _BASE_DAMAGE * fake_upgrade_level` (3, 6, 9, ...), which is the same sequence -- and the sim's form is strictly better behaved, because `fake_upgrade_level` is re-seeded in `_init_vars` so a downgrade cannot corrupt it (contrast card/maul, card/rampage and card/thrash, which mutate their damage in place and lose it). What is missing is only the STORAGE SHAPE: there is no `_damage` attribute, so `Card.base_damage` (cards/base.py:191-195) returns None and the observation encoder sees no damage for Wither even though `damage` is right at the use site. The PROP SET is reproduced correctly: the sim passes no explicit props and `DamageCmd.deal` infers `DamageProps.CARD_UNPOWERED` (UNPOWERED | MOVE) from `is_unpowered = True` (cmds.py:44-50, wither.py:154), so the damage is not Strength-scaled and IS blockable on both sides -- identical to card/burn, card/decay, card/infection and card/toxic. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's printed-number API cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnTurnEndInHand.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Damage, this)` (Wither.cs:59) -- passing the VAR so the props ride along -- == `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self.damage, dealer=None, card=self)`. Explicit null dealer on both sides, and the amount is the fake-upgraded value on both.

OnPlay.rationale: Wither.cs declares no OnPlay and the card is Unplayable.

guards.what: FakeUpgrade is a plain public method, not an override, so the harness does not enumerate it (Wither.cs:62-66)
guards.rationale: `FakeUpgradeLevel++` plus `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` == the sim's `fake_upgrade()` incrementing `fake_upgrade_level` (wither.py:167-169), with the damage following from the property. The Aeonglass boss's "Increasing Intensity" move is the caller and belongs to the monster stream; the sim's docstring records that it fake-upgrades every existing Wither and matches newly generated ones to its count.
